items.title: Asia stocks mixed as chip rout triggers KOSPI trading halt; China outperforms
items.summary: Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed on Thursday, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor shares triggered a trading curb in South Korea, offsetting support from a steep decline in oil prices after Democrats' victories in the U.S. midterm elections.

items.title: Oil holds steep losses after U.S. election fuels Iran peace hopes
items.summary: Investing.com-- Oil prices held largely steady in Asian trading on Thursday after plunging more than 8% in the previous session, as investors weighed the prospect that Democrats' sweeping victory in U.S. midterm elections could increase pressure on President Donald Trump to end the war with Iran.

items.title: UAE weighs third crude pipeline to bypass Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: Investing.com -- The United Arab Emirates is evaluating plans to construct a third crude export conduit to its eastern coast, according to reporting from Bloomberg, as Abu Dhabi accelerates a multibillion-dollar strategic pivot designed to bypass the volatile Strait of Hormuz entirely. items.title: Has the global oil market returned to surplus? JPMorgan thinks so
items.summary: Investing.com -- The global oil market has returned to a surplus after months of supply disruptions linked to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, with recovering Middle Eastern exports and rising production in Latin America bringing more crude back into circulation, JPMorgan said.

items.title: Inflation Is Running Above 3%. These 3 Dividend Stocks Have the Pricing Power to Keep Up.
items.summary: When inflation eats into your dividend's buying power, pricing power becomes the one trait separating stocks that keep up from those that quietly fall behind. Three consumer giants are charging more and still selling more, and the gap between them matters more than most investors realize.
